targets: x402-foundation/x402#3389 — {alg, enc, hex} canonical digest triple
vauban-org/x402-starknet — v3 foreign-leaf (digest_lo, digest_hi), felt252 masking

rules.triple: Every digest carried in a record is {alg, enc, hex}. `alg` names the digest function. `enc` names the storage encoding a verifier MUST apply before comparing. A record that omits `enc` is INVALID rather than defaulted (seritalien, x402#3389, 2026-09-08).
rules.felt252_mask: On Starknet a 256-bit digest is stored as a 251-bit field element: stored = D & ((1 << 251) - 1). A verifier that compares the FULL digest against the stored value reports a false negative on 31 of every 32 digests, because the top 5 bits are only all-zero 1 time in 32.
rules.limbs: Vauban v3 foreign leaf splits a 256-bit digest big-endian: digest_lo = D mod 2^128, digest_hi = D >> 128. Order is low-then-high.

cases.description: Unmasked digest. enc:none means the hex IS the comparison value; limbs must round-trip losslessly.
cases.provenance: Real StillOS Notary production receipt, resolved_verdict, ledger line 2283, ts 2026-09-06T17:20:11.994Z. Not a synthetic fixture.

cases.description: THE LOAD-BEARING CASE. Same digest stored as a felt252. Top 5 bits are 0b01100 (=12), so masking CHANGES the value. An implementation that ignores enc will compare the wrong bytes here.

expect.note: A verifier comparing full == stored FAILS here. That failure is correct behaviour to detect, not a bug in the vector.

cases.description: The 1-in-32 digest whose top 5 bits are already zero, so masking is a no-op and a BROKEN verifier still passes. Included specifically so a suite cannot accidentally validate a broken implementation by testing only one digest.
cases.provenance: sha256('stillos-conformance-probe-15'), found by search. Deterministic and independently reproducible.

expect.note: Passing this case alone proves nothing. It must be run together with triple-02.

cases.description: A record omitting enc MUST be rejected, not defaulted to none. This is the explicit normative rule from x402#3389.
An unlabelled digest invites fake cross-ledger agreement — sha256 and keccak256 are indistinguishable by display. goun7/Tamga hit this in practice (x402#3389, 2026-09-07).
An unrecognised enc must fail closed rather than being treated as none.
A 256-bit digest must be exactly 64 hex chars. Truncation must not be silently zero-padded.

Tamga-shaped chain head: a plain SHA-256 over a deterministic JCS encoding, carried as enc:none, dropping into a batch leaf with no protocol surgery. Demonstrates the triple is implementation-neutral.
cases.provenance: Shape only, per goun7's description in x402#3389. Not a real Tamga head — Tamga's own verified head does not exist yet (gated behind their #3379 pilot). Marked synthetic deliberately.
